revisions.purpose: Web-only change, no version bump: where a name on the Tc chart sits, and the preprint swatch in the legend. Mercury's 4.2 K lies exactly on the liquid-helium line and the record staircase starts at the same dot, so a name level with it lay across both; MgB2 sat above and well left of its dot on a phone. Every spot is now scored and the lowest wins, rather than the first that fits: distance to the nearest edge of the box plus a quarter of the distance to its middle, which keeps a long name from hanging off one end of its own dot, with extra cost for sitting nearer another material's dot than its own and for lying across a line. The close centred spots are in the listed set now, and the five era-opening names are placed most-crowded-first, since placed fourth MgB2 found its neighbourhood taken. A narrow chart is 430 px tall, not 330. Mercury now sits below its dot and clear of both lines at every width, MgB2 directly below at 560 px and above; on a phone MgB2 stays about sixteen pixels up and left because every nearer spot would cover one of the twenty-five dots around it. Names placed went 38 to 41 at 1100 px and 18 to 25 at 414. Separately, the legend's preprint swatch was a ten pixel box with a dashed CSS border and a round corner radius, which browsers lay out one side at a time, drawing four lopsided arcs instead of a dashed ring; it is an SVG circle now, like the dot it stands for, with pathLength set so the dashes come out even. The data, the models and the results are unchanged.
